# GATE locate-policy text: authorship → install → templates → MCP header

## 1. Problem restatement

Scubiee ships a dense "GATE" locate policy (Prefer Scubiee for soft/structural
lookups, Forbid-first Grep/Glob for literals/names, an enrich-query→map→pack
ladder, and FAIL conditions for skipping `pack_context`). This text appears in
`AGENTS.md`, `.kiro/steering/scubiee.md`, `.cursor/rules/scubiee.mdc`, and the
live MCP server `instructions` field. The question: where is the canonical
wording authored in code, how is it wrapped into a `GATE {line}` block and
written into `AGENTS.md`/sibling files, how do the Cursor/Kiro templates carry
the `GATE 1` line, how does the MCP header reinforce the same policy every
turn, and where does the always-apply Cursor rule actually land on disk.

## 2. Ordered call/flow narrative

1. **Text authorship (single source, two variants)** — `packages/pipeline/rules_installer.py`
   defines the canonical policy prose in two sibling functions:
   - `managed_gate_usage_short()` (loc 53-99) — the CLI/general-surface variant
     ("Prefer CLI `scubiee map`→`pack --mode lean`→`expand`... else MCP `map`→`pack_context`...").
   - `managed_gate_mcp_only_usage_short()` (loc ~100-131, right after the first)
     — the MCP-only variant used for Kiro steering and this repo's AGENTS.md/
     `.kiro/steering/scubiee.md` ("**MUST Use Scubiee MCP for locate**... BAN
     shell `scubiee map|pack|expand` on this MCP-only surface..."). This is the
     exact text observed verbatim in this workspace's `AGENTS.md` and
     `.kiro/steering/scubiee.md`.
   Both bodies share the same skeleton: MUST-use line → "Prefer host first
   (Forbid-first map/pack)" bullets → "WHEN SCUBIEE (MCP) IS AVAILABLE —
   STRICT, NO ESCAPE" bullets (enrich-query sizing, map→pack requirement,
   refine-with-suggested_seed, FAIL conditions, budget ≤3 calls, BAN
   whole-file Read).

2. **Wrapping into a GATE block** — Still in `rules_installer.py`:
   - `managed_gate_rule_body(gate_line, project_id)` (loc ~195-199) wraps
     `managed_gate_usage_short()` with a header:
     `f"**GATE {gate_line}** - Managed repo. \`project_id={project_id!r}\`.\n\n{body}"`.
   - `managed_gate_mcp_only_rule_body(gate_line, project_id)` does the same but
     wraps `managed_gate_mcp_only_usage_short()` — this is the function whose
     output matches this workspace's GATE text exactly (`**GATE 1:ce_…** -
     Managed repo. project_id='ce_…'.` followed by the MCP-only bullets).
   - Non-managed states: `unmanaged_gate_rule_body(gate_line="0")` (BAN Scubiee
     MCP locate, native-only) and `paused_gate_rule_body()` (`GATE p`, BAN all
     Scubiee MCP tools, "Run `scubiee resume`").
   - `gate_line_for_repo(repo)` (loc ~320-334) computes which gate line to use:
     checks `pipeline.pause_resume.is_paused()` → `"p"`; else
     `pipeline.project_id.read_id_file(root)` → `f"1:{pid}"`; else `"0"`.

3. **Writing into AGENTS.md** — `write_project_gate_rules(repo, dry_run=False, slugs=None)`
   (loc 1207-1270) is the entry point run after `scubiee init`/`connect`:
   - Computes `gate = gate_line_for_repo(root)`; bails out (`skipped`) if the
     folder isn't project-rules-eligible (`_project_rules_eligible`, loc
     337-343: needs `.scubiee/id.json` or `.git`) or gate is neither `1:...`
     nor `p`.
   - Iterates `TOOL_MAP.values()` (or a filtered `slugs` subset) from
     `pipeline.tool_registry`, and for each tool with `rule_format != "none"`,
     writes to every path from `resolve_rule_project_paths(tool, root)` via
     `_write_rule(tool, path, gate_line=gate)`.
   - Then unconditionally writes/append to `root / "AGENTS.md"` via
     `_write_rule_append_md(agents, gate_line=gate)`.
   - `_write_rule_append_md(path, gate_line)` (loc ~1177-1190): strips any
     previous `_MARKER_START.._MARKER_END` block via `_strip_marked_sections`
     (loc 1352-1363), computes `content = _rule_content_md(gate_line=gate)`,
     wraps it as `f"{_MARKER_START}\n{content}\n{_MARKER_END}\n"`, and appends
     it to the file (creating it if missing). `_MARKER_START`/`_MARKER_END`
     are imported from `pipeline.branding` and are the literal
     `<!-- scubiee:start -->` / `<!-- scubiee:end -->` HTML comments visible in
     this workspace's `AGENTS.md`.
   - `_rule_content_md(gate_line)` → if `gate_line` truthy, calls
     `_render_gate_rule_md(gate_line)` (loc ~311-317), which dispatches on the
     gate line prefix: `"p"` → `paused_gate_rule_body()`; starts with `"1:"` →
     `managed_gate_rule_body(gate_line, pid)`; else →
     `unmanaged_gate_rule_body(gate_line)`. (Note: for plain `AGENTS.md` this
     uses the **CLI-flavored** `managed_gate_usage_short`, not the MCP-only
     one — the MCP-only body is reserved for Kiro-steering-shaped paths,
     see step 4.)

4. **Per-tool rule dispatch (`_write_rule` / `_RULE_WRITERS`)** — `rules_installer.py`
   defines three writer functions keyed by `tool.rule_format` in
   `_RULE_WRITERS = {"mdc": _write_rule_mdc, "md": _write_rule_md,
   "append-md": _write_rule_append_md, "none": lambda *_: None}`:
   - `_write_rule_mdc(path, gate_line)` (loc ~1153-1159 area, just above
     `_write_rule_md`): writes `_rule_content_mdc(gate_line=gate_line)`
     directly (idempotent — skips write if unchanged). Used for Cursor
     (`rule_format="mdc"`).
   - `_write_rule_md(path, gate_line)` (right after `_write_rule_mdc`): checks
     `is_kiro_steering = "steering" in path.parts (lowered) and
     path.name.lower().startswith("scubiee")`. If it's Kiro steering AND
     `gate_line` starts with `"1:"`, it builds
     `content = managed_gate_mcp_only_rule_body(gate_line, pid) + "\n"` and
     prefixes `"---\ninclusion: always\n---\n\n"` (an always-loaded Kiro
     steering frontmatter) — **this is the exact mechanism that produces the
     MCP-only GATE text seen in `.kiro/steering/scubiee.md`** in this
     workspace. Otherwise it falls back to `_rule_content_md(gate_line)` (same
     CLI-flavored body as AGENTS.md), still frontmatter-wrapped if under
     `steering/`.
   - `_write_rule_append_md` — described in step 3 (used for AGENTS.md-style
     targets: Claude's `CLAUDE.md`, Codex's `AGENTS.md`, Copilot's
     instructions, OpenCode/Amp/Pi `AGENTS.md`, etc., per `rule_format`).

5. **Cursor `.mdc` template + `write_cursor_rule`** — `packages/pipeline/mcp_install.py`:
   - `_context_agent_rule_template()` (loc ~256-260) points at
     `pipeline/templates/scubiee.mdc` (the on-disk fallback/overview template
     asset — not the primary write path for the *live* rule, which is
     generated).
   - `write_cursor_rule(repo=None)` (loc 262-271): resolves
     `dest = target / ".cursor" / "rules" / "scubiee.mdc"`, computes
     `gate = gate_line_for_repo(target)`, and writes
     `_rule_content_mdc(gate_line=gate)` to `dest`. Docstring: "Write repo rule
     with real `GATE 1:ce_…` (included every chat by Cursor)." Called from
     `write_cursor_mcp()` right after the project `mcp.json` is merged, so
     Cursor gets both MCP wiring and the always-apply rule in one connect
     pass.
   - `_rule_content_mdc(gate_line)` (rules_installer.py ~loc 271-274) →
     `_render_gate_rule_mdc(gate_line)` (~loc 283-308): builds YAML frontmatter
     `description: GATE {gate_line} Scubiee managed` / `alwaysApply: true`,
     then body = `managed_gate_rule_body(gate_line, pid)` for `"1:"` lines
     (same CLI-flavored usage_short as AGENTS.md, **not** the MCP-only
     variant — Cursor's rule text differs slightly from Kiro's steering text
     for this reason).
   - Fallback when no live `gate_line`: `gate_overview_mdc()` /
     `gate_overview_md()` (loc ~236-258) render all three states
     (unmanaged/managed/paused) as bullets using
     `managed_gate_overview_bullet()` (loc ~179-192, `**GATE 1:ce_***`
     placeholder text for docs/templates before a real project_id exists).

6. **MCP server instructions (reinforced every turn)** — `packages/pipeline/mcp_locate.py`:
   - `_phase_experiment()` (loc 72-87) reads `CTX_MCP_EXPERIMENT` env var to
     pick `"classic"` / `"lab"` / `"ship"` (default).
   - `_phase_server_instructions()` (loc 283-313, calling into module-level
     `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_PHASE_*_BODY` string constants defined just above
     it): builds `header = managed_gate_mcp_header()` (imported from
     `rules_installer.py`, loc 141-176) — a *short* per-experiment
     reinforcement string ("LOCATE PRIORITY: soft/structural → Prefer
     map→pack_context...; WHEN SCUBIEE AVAILABLE — STRICT, NO ESCAPE: MUST
     pack — map-only/warming ≠ skip..."). Then selects a longer `body`
     constant (`SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_PHASE_SHIP_BODY` by default) containing
     the full incremental ladder how-to (ENRICH → map(k=10) → pack_context
     (mode=lean) → Native-Read → expand_context/collect_hot_context, plus
     query-quality examples and Forbid-first exceptions).
   - Final assembly: `f"Scubiee MCP locate ({label}; CTX_MCP_EXPERIMENT={exp}). Tools: {tools}.\n" + header + "\n\n" + body`.
   - **Design split confirmed by comments in code**: "Layering (research-
     backed): Rules = WHEN/PRIORITY/ESCAPE (no tool recipes). MCP instructions
     = WHAT each tool is for + query tip." So the GATE rule files (AGENTS.md/
     steering/mdc) carry the *policy* (`managed_gate_usage_short` /
     `managed_gate_mcp_only_usage_short`), while the MCP server's
     `instructions` field carries the *header* (`managed_gate_mcp_header`,
     tiny, injected every turn) + the *phase-ship body* (the actual
     step-by-step how-to). The header intentionally duplicates the
     Prefer/Forbid gist so it survives even if an agent's rule files aren't
     loaded; the body is the "how" that rule text explicitly says not to
     duplicate.

# Retrieval context pack — Scubiee managed GATE locate policy: authorship → install → runtime reinforcement

## Problem restatement (≤8 lines)
Trace how the "managed GATE" locate policy (Prefer/Forbid host-vs-Scubiee rules, enrich-query
requirement, map→pack ladder) is (1) authored once in Python string-builder functions, (2) wrapped
into GATE blocks written to `AGENTS.md` and sibling agent files, (3) mirrored into Cursor/Kiro
overview templates (`scubiee.md` / `scubiee.mdc`) as a "GATE 1" bullet, (4) re-emitted inside the
live MCP server's `instructions` string every session (prefix header + phase body split), and
(5) how the Cursor project rule (`.cursor/rules/scubiee.mdc`, `alwaysApply: true`) gets installed
via `write_cursor_rule`. All evidence below is retrieved directly from source in this workspace
(native `rg`/file reads only — no Scubiee CLI/MCP used, per task constraints).

## Ordered call/flow narrative

1. **Single source of truth (authoring).** `packages/pipeline/rules_installer.py` defines a family
   of pure string-builder functions that are the *only* place the Prefer/Forbid + enrich-query +
   map→pack ladder wording lives:
   - `managed_gate_usage_short()` — CLI/general surface wording (native `scubiee map|pack|expand`
     mentioned alongside MCP names).
   - `managed_gate_mcp_only_usage_short()` — MCP-only surface wording (Kiro steering / A-B
     with-arm), same policy, MCP tool names only, bans shell `scubiee map|pack|expand`.
   - `managed_gate_mcp_header()` — compact ~80–110 word reinforcement string returned by
     `CTX_MCP_EXPERIMENT` variant (`classic` / `lab` / default `ship`); meant to be re-embedded in
     MCP server instructions every session.
   - `managed_gate_overview_bullet()` — the "GATE 1:ce_*" one-paragraph bullet used when no live
     `project_id` is known yet (overview/fallback templates).
   These four functions are explicitly documented in the module docstring/comment block
   (`# Shared GATE policy — single source for templates, written rules, and MCP header.`) as the
   canonical layering: *Rules = WHEN/PRIORITY/ESCAPE; MCP instructions = WHAT + query tip; tool
   results = data only.*

2. **Wrapping into a GATE line + rule body.** Still in `rules_installer.py`:
   - `managed_gate_rule_body(gate_line, project_id)` → wraps `managed_gate_usage_short()` under a
     `**GATE {gate_line}** - Managed repo. project_id=...` heading (general/native surface).
   - `managed_gate_mcp_only_rule_body(gate_line, project_id)` → same wrapper but calls
     `managed_gate_mcp_only_usage_short()` (MCP-only surface, e.g. Kiro steering).
   - `unmanaged_gate_rule_body()` (GATE 0, not enrolled) and `paused_gate_rule_body()` (GATE p,
     `scubiee stop`) are sibling wrappers for the other two lifecycle states, using the constant
     `PAUSED_AGENT_BAN`.
   - `_render_gate_rule_md(gate_line)` / `_render_gate_rule_mdc(gate_line)` dispatch on the gate
     line (`"p"`, `"1:<pid>"`, else `"0"`) to pick the right wrapper and, for `.mdc`, add Cursor
     frontmatter (`alwaysApply: true`).
   - `gate_overview_md()` / `gate_overview_mdc()` render *all three* GATE states concatenated —
     this is the fallback used when no live `project_id` exists yet, and it is byte-identical to
     the checked-in template files (`packages/pipeline/templates/scubiee.md` /
     `packages/pipeline/templates/scubiee.mdc`), confirming these templates are generated/kept in
     sync with the same builder functions, not hand-authored docs.

3. **Install into `AGENTS.md` and sibling agent files.**
   - `write_project_gate_rules(repo, ...)` (in `rules_installer.py`) is the top-level "apply GATE
     to a repo" entry point. It computes `gate = gate_line_for_repo(root)` (reads
     `.scubiee/id.json` via `pipeline.project_id.read_id_file`, or `"p"` if
     `pipeline.pause_resume.is_paused()`), then for every connected tool with `rule_format != "none"`
     calls `_write_rule(tool, path, gate_line=gate)`, and **always** additionally calls
     `_write_rule_append_md(root / "AGENTS.md", gate_line=gate)`.
   - `_write_rule_append_md` strips any previously-marked Scubiee section
     (`_strip_marked_sections`, delimited by `MARKER_START`/`MARKER_END` from `pipeline.branding`)
     and appends a fresh `{MARKER_START}\n{content}\n{MARKER_END}\n` block, where `content` is
     `_rule_content_md(gate_line=gate)` → `_render_gate_rule_md(gate_line)` →
     `managed_gate_rule_body(...)`. This exact mechanism is what produced the
     `<!-- scubiee:start --> ... <!-- scubiee:end -->` block visible at the top of this
     workspace's own `AGENTS.md` (the GATE text there is the with-Scubiee-disabled variant, i.e.
     this A/B "without" arm ships a hand-frozen ban block instead of a live-rendered one — see
     Open Questions).
   - `_write_rule` dispatches on `tool.rule_format` (`"mdc" | "md" | "append-md" | "none"`) via the
     `_RULE_WRITERS` dict to one of `_write_rule_mdc` / `_write_rule_md` / `_write_rule_append_md`.
   - `_write_rule_md` has a special case for Kiro: if the path lives under a `steering/` directory
     and starts with `scubiee`, and `gate_line` starts with `"1:"`, it uses
     `managed_gate_mcp_only_rule_body` (MCP-only wording) instead of the general
     `managed_gate_rule_body`, and always prefixes Kiro content with
     `---\ninclusion: always\n---\n\n` frontmatter — this is why
     `.kiro/steering/scubiee.md` is the MCP-only phrasing while `AGENTS.md` (append-md format)
     uses the general/native phrasing.

4. **Fan-out across every connected tool + every managed repo.**
   - `apply_connected_tools_to_repo(repo)` — called after `scubiee init` from
     `packages/pipeline/repo_lifecycle.py` line ~456-458 (inside the enroll/reconcile function) —
     loads `load_connected_tools()` (from `pipeline.connect_state`), checks `gate_line_for_repo`,
     and for each connected tool slug calls `write_project_tool_surface(root, tool)`, then finally
     calls `write_project_gate_rules(root, slugs=slugs)` once more for the AGENTS.md block.
   - `write_project_tool_surface(repo, tool)` writes the MCP pin (`_write_workspace_mcp`) **and**
     the GATE rule (`write_project_gate_rules(root, slugs=[tool.slug])`) **and** applies MCP tool
     permissions (`pipeline.mcp_permissions.apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface`) for that one
     tool.
   - `install_tool(tool, ...)` (also in `rules_installer.py`, used by `scubiee connect --<tool>`,
     wired from `packages/pipeline/__main__.py` `cmd_connect` → `from pipeline.rules_installer
     import install_tools`) removes stale legacy-global MCP entries, then calls
     `fan_out_tool_to_enrolled_repos(tool)`, which iterates every enrolled repo in the local
     registry (`pipeline.managed_repos.managed_repo_paths`) and calls
     `write_project_tool_surface` for each — this is how one `connect` invocation propagates the
     GATE block + MCP pin to *every* previously-enrolled repo, not just the CWD.

5. **Cursor `.mdc` project rule / `write_cursor_rule`.**
   - `packages/pipeline/tool_registry.py` defines the Cursor `ToolDef` with
     `rule_format="mdc"` and `rule_user_path=".cursor/rules/scubiee.mdc"` — this is the
     `resolve_rule_project_paths` target that `_write_rule_mdc` writes to during
     `write_project_gate_rules`/`apply_connected_tools_to_repo`.
   - Separately, `packages/pipeline/mcp_install.py` defines `write_cursor_rule(repo=None)`
     (older/adjacent code path, used by `write_cursor_mcp`, which is invoked by legacy/manual
     Cursor MCP-merge flows): it computes `dest = repo/.cursor/rules/scubiee.mdc` and writes
     `_rule_content_mdc(gate_line=gate_line_for_repo(target))` — i.e. it **imports the same
     renderer from `rules_installer.py`** rather than re-implementing the GATE text, so both entry
     points (the `connect`/`init` fan-out and the standalone `write_cursor_mcp` helper) always
     produce byte-identical `.mdc` content.
   - The rendered `.mdc` always carries Cursor frontmatter `alwaysApply: true` (see
     `_render_gate_rule_mdc` and the static fallback `gate_overview_mdc()` / the checked-in
     `templates/scubiee.mdc`), which is what makes Cursor always inject the rule regardless of
     file glob context — this satisfies "always-apply Cursor rule."

6. **MCP server instructions — header vs phase-ship body, reinforced every session.**
   - `packages/pipeline/mcp_locate.py::create_mcp()` builds
     `FastMCP(name, instructions=_server_instructions(surface))` — the MCP protocol
     `instructions` field, sent once at server/session initialize (not literally re-sent per tool
     call by the protocol, but re-computed fresh every time the server process starts / a client
     reconnects, and hosts that keep it in context effectively treat it as "every turn").
   - `_server_instructions(surface)`: for gate `"p"` returns the paused ban string; otherwise
     computes `prefix = _gate_instruction_prefix(gate)` (→ just `f"GATE {g}. "`) and picks a `body`
     from a dict keyed by `surface` (`"graph" | "rich" | "search" | "grep" | "nav" | "phase"`),
     defaulting to `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_READ`; for `surface == "phase"` the body is
     `_phase_server_instructions()`.
   - `_phase_server_instructions()` is the "header vs body" composition point: it calls
     `header = managed_gate_mcp_header()` (imported from `rules_installer`, the compact per-`exp`
     variant string) and appends `body` = one of `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_PHASE_SHIP_BODY` /
     `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_PHASE_CLASSIC_BODY` / `SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_PHASE_LAB_BODY` (chosen via
     `CTX_MCP_EXPERIMENT` env var), returning
     `f"Scubiee MCP locate ({label}; ...). Tools: {tools}.\n{header}\n\n{body}"`. So the *header*
     is always the shared `managed_gate_mcp_header()` policy line, and the *phase ship body* is
     the longer scenario/ladder/exceptions essay (`SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS_PHASE_SHIP_BODY`,
     ~40 lines, defined just above `_phase_server_instructions`) — this is the literal
     "header vs phase ship body" split named in the task.
   - Separately from the one-time `instructions=` string, **every individual tool JSON response**
     carries a compact one-token gate reinforcement: `attach_gate_lean()` in
     `packages/pipeline/mcp_response_lean.py` sets `out.setdefault("g", gate_line(just_checked=False))`
     on every response card, called from `mcp_locate.py::_attach_gate()` (line ~2334) which wraps
     every tool's return value via `_format()`. This is the true "reinforce every turn" mechanism
     — a `"g": "1:ce_xxxx"` (or `"0"`/`"p"`) field riding on every tool call result, independent of
     the one-time server `instructions` string.
